intro: Top-k decoding restricts which tokens can be sampled before renormalizing their probabilities. Looking at the distribution makes the effects of truncation, temperature and ties visible.
task: Return the token probability vector after selecting exactly k candidates. Keep the operation deterministic so you can inspect the distribution without relying on a lucky random sample.
requirements: logits is a nonempty one-dimensional real array. k is an integer in [1,len(logits)], excluding booleans. Require temperature>=1e-6.
Keep exactly the k largest logits. Resolve ties by lower original index first. Assign zero probability to every excluded token.

Apply a stable softmax to retained logits divided by temperature and return a new vector with the same shape as logits. This function returns probabilities; it neither samples a token nor applies nucleus/top-p filtering.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Select indices before normalizing
hints.body: The selected logits must be renormalized among themselves after the other candidates are excluded.

hints.title: Specify tie behavior
hints.body: A value threshold can retain more than k tokens when several logits share the kth value. Stable sorting gives an exact candidate count.

explanation: Temperature changes relative probabilities within the retained set. It does not change the ranking when positive, and k=1 always produces a one-hot distribution.
A smaller candidate set can remove plausible tokens. Returning the whole probability vector lets you see that tradeoff without interpreting individual random draws.

Adapted the upstream top-k and temperature steps while removing top-p filtering and random sampling. Unlike its threshold-based tie handling, this contract retains exactly k indices with stable index-order ties.
